composio.note: Kintone REST is in Composio's bring-your-own-OAuth-app list; create the auth config with your client ID and secret.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio does not manage a Kintone OAuth app, so you must register an OAuth client in Kintone and give Composio its client ID and secret.
reasons: Composio has no managed Kintone app
Consent screen shows your client name
Scopes are set per request, so you control access

scenarios.label: Agent acting in customers' Kintone domains
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent connects to end users' Kintone domains using an OAuth client and the Authorization Code flow.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: No provider review or timeline found; the customer admin's enablement time is not documented.

scenarios.approval: No provider review was found. The client is registered inside a Kintone domain, and its admin must enable it for users.

prerequisites.title: Kintone domain with admin access
prerequisites.detail: Registering the client needs the User & System Administration page.

prerequisites.title: Public redirect endpoint
prerequisites.detail: You need a redirect URL for the client. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Open Kintone OAuth settings
steps.detail: Log in as admin, open the gear icon, go to User & System Administration, then OAuth.
steps.done_when: The Add OAuth Client button is visible.

steps.title: Get the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard for the Kintone REST toolkit.
steps.done_when: You have the redirect URI string.

steps.title: Add the OAuth client
steps.detail: Enter a client name, an optional logo, and the redirect endpoint, then click Save.
steps.done_when: Client ID and client secret are shown.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config for kintone_rest through Composio's API with your client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists in Composio.

steps.title: Enable the client for users
steps.detail: Click Configure users next to the client and tick each user who may connect.

steps.title: Test the connection
steps.detail: Connect a test user and approve the authorization request, with the scope requested such as k:app_record:read.
steps.done_when: A token is returned and a record read succeeds.

traps.title: Users are disabled by default
traps.detail: A new client has no users enabled, and each newly created Kintone user is unchecked by default. Connections fail until the admin ticks them.

traps.title: IP restrictions block the client
traps.detail: Domains with IP restrictions cannot use OAuth clients unless the client's IP is whitelisted.

traps.title: Access tokens last one hour
traps.detail: Expired codes or tokens return errors. Refresh tokens do not expire, but at most 10 per client per user.

traps.title: Scopes must be requested explicitly
traps.detail: A token only works for APIs in its scope; separate multiple scopes with spaces.

blockers.what_it_means: The Kintone admin has not enabled the client for that user.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the admin to tick the user under Configure users.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft instructions for the customer's admin.

blockers.symptom: Authorization code or token returns an error
blockers.what_it_means: The code (10 minutes) or access token (1 hour) expired.
blockers.what_to_do: Restart authorization or use the refresh token.
